title: Belfast radicals start a republican movement
spotify: In Our Time The Irish Rebellion of 1798
description: Melvyn Bragg’s In Our Time on the 1798 rising led by the United Irishmen, a society founded by Belfast Presbyterian radicals in 1791. Henry Joy McCracken, hanged in the city that July, is remembered in Clifton Street Cemetery.

title: Cups of Armada gold come ashore in a museum
episode: When the Spanish Armada Reached Ireland
spotify: Not Just the Tudors When the Spanish Armada Reached Ireland
description: Historian Suzannah Lipscomb and Michael B. Barry on the Spanish Armada ships wrecked on Ireland’s coast in 1588. Gold and jewels raised from one of them, the Girona, lost off the Antrim coast, are shown at the Ulster Museum.

title: A city library older than the city hall
episode: Exploring “Belfast’s Great Shared Space” with The Linen Hall’s Julie Andrews
place: Linen Hall Library, Donegall Square North
spotify: Irish Stew Podcast Exploring Belfast's Great Shared Space with The Linen Hall's Julie Andrews
description: Julie Andrews, director of the Linen Hall Library, talks about Belfast’s oldest cultural institution, founded in 1788 and now in a Victorian linen warehouse facing City Hall. Its first librarian was United Irishman Thomas Russell.

title: An orphan from Belfast becomes a society painter
episode: [Documentary] Sir John Lavery: "The Belfast Orphan Who Painted History"
spotify: Best Of Belfast Sir John Lavery The Belfast Orphan Who Painted History
description: Painter Sir John Lavery, born in Belfast in 1856 and orphaned young, became a leading portraitist of his day, painting Churchill and Michael Collins. He was baptised in St Patrick’s Church on Donegall Street, which holds a triptych he gave it.

title: Shipyard workers win a cup in Vienna
episode: Glentoran FC and the Vienna Cup, with Sam Robinson
spotify: Historical Belfast Glentoran FC and the Vienna Cup, with Sam Robinson
description: Just before the First World War, a Glentoran FC side of industrial workers from Ballymacarrett, the terraced district by the shipyards, travelled to Vienna and won its cup. Sam Robinson tells the story. Glentoran still plays at The Oval stadium.

title: A heart doctor puts a defibrillator in an ambulance
description: In 1966 cardiologist Frank Pantridge of Belfast’s Royal Victoria Hospital launched the world’s first mobile coronary care unit, an ambulance carrying a portable defibrillator run off car batteries. BBC Witness History tells how it started.

title: Van Morrison’s east Belfast, street by street
episode: 836 Van Morrison's Belfast; Roma in Europe; Classic European Hikes
spotify: Travel with Rick Steves 836 Van Morrison's Belfast
description: In the opening segment of Rick Steves’ radio show, a Belfast guide points out the places that shaped singer Van Morrison, born in 1945 at 125 Hyndford Street in east Belfast, and the streets and parks he named in his songs.
